content: mae (PM): Quick design check — I'm worried the new compact roles grid feels too dense on smaller screens. Thoughts? :thinking_face: josh (frontend): Agree, on 1024px it becomes two cramped columns. Can we hide non-critical columns under a breakpoint? :eyes: ananya (designer): Proposal: collapse 'Last activity' + 'Notes' into a kebab menu per row on < 1200px. Keep role name, members, and primary actions. Sketch attached: https://figma.redwood/app/roles-compact?v=3 rory (a11y): Important: if we collapse into a menu, keyboard users must be able to open it via `Enter`/`Space` and the menu items need `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`. Also contrast on the role badges is low — WCAG AA failing on some combos. lina (eng): Implementation note — collapsing into a per-row menu is fine, but watch for perf on large orgs (10k rows). We should lazy-render menus and use virtualization. mae (PM): Good call on perf. Ananya, can we run a quick content-priority pass to decide what is critical vs secondary? ananya (designer): Yep. Critical: Role name, member count, primary actions (edit/disable). Secondary: Last activity, owner, notes. Secondary goes into menu. Also copy tweak suggestion for SSO toggle: current label 'SSO enforcement' -> suggest 'Require SSO to sign in' (clearer). josh (frontend): Love that copy. For the toggle microcopy, let's also add a tooltip: "When enabled, users must sign in using your SSO provider." rory (a11y): Tooltip must be accessible: prefer a visually hidden accessible description linked via `aria-describedby`. Example: ```html When enabled, users must sign in using your SSO provider. Enabling this will block password sign-ins. ``` pete (qa): Also found an edge-case in audit log nav: when you filter by org > role change and then press back, the focus jumps to top, not to the filter chip. We should preserve focus and URL state. lina (eng): Agree, we'll persist filters in query params (`?filter=role_change&since=30d`) and restore focus to the first active chip on back navigation. mae (PM): UX questions: 1) Should 'Require SSO' be an org-level toggle or per-org + per-seat? 2) How obvious is the enforcement consequence in the invite flow? ananya (designer): My take: org-level toggle for enforcement default, but per-invite override allowed for special cases (with clear inline warning). In the invite modal, show a warning banner when org requires SSO: "This org requires SSO; invited users must sign in with SSO." Small link to learn more. josh (frontend): For the invite modal, avoid modal stacking. If we need extra explanation, use an inline expanding info panel instead of a new modal. rory (a11y): Accessibility nit: the invite modal's form fields lack `aria-invalid` on validation errors; also focus order on the permission matrix is wrong — skip buttons appear before inputs. Need to audit with keyboard walkthrough. pete (qa): I'll write a short regression checklist: keyboard tab flow, aria attributes present, tooltip screenreader text, URL filter restore, and color contrast checks for badges >= 4.5:1. mae (PM): Timeline? Lina/Josh can we get a small spike for collapse + virtualization and an a11y checklist by EOD Fri? lina (eng): Spike + prototype by Fri morning. Will add perf numbers. josh (frontend): I'll pair with Lina on the prototype. ananya (designer): I'll push updated mocks and copy edits tonight, will include accessible tooltip markup suggestions. rory (a11y): I'll start a voiceover + keyboard test doc and ping folks for review. mae (PM): Perfect. One last tiny copy nit: change 'Manage SSO' CTA in settings sidebar to 'SSO & authentication' — users looked for that phrasing in research. ananya (designer): Noted, will update. pete (qa): I'll slot regression tests after spike validation next week. mae (PM): Thanks all :thumbsup:
